title: Prospective observational study on the effectiveness of a new capsulated mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) for pulpotomies and indirect pulp capping in primary and permanent teeth: 12 months follow-up
summary:
Preserving the vitality of the dental pulp in primary and permanent teeth affected by deep carious lesions or traumatic fractures is crucial for long-term dental health. While Mineral Trioxide Aggregate (MTA) is widely recognized for its superior biocompatibility and sealing ability, the preparation of conventional MTA can be time-consuming. 
The objective of the present study is to evaluate the clinical and radiological success rates of an encapsulated mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA vpt, VOCO GmbH, Germany) used for pulpotomies and indirect pulp capping in both primary and permanent teeth. These treatments are indicated as a result of deep caries or dental trauma and were recommended to the patients by their treating dentist independently of the present project. Depending on the clinical findings and the type of tooth (primary or permanent), a pulp-preserving measure (either pulpotomy or indirect pulp capping) is performed. In the case of a pulpotomy, the coronal portion of the dental pulp is removed, subsequently covered with MTA, and completed with a definitive restoration (filling or crown). In indirect pulp capping, the same material (MTA vpt, VOCO GmbH, Germany) is applied to protect the dental pulp, for example, following selective caries removal. The treated teeth are then closely monitored clinically and radiologically at 6- and 12-month intervals during regular dental check-ups and prophylaxis appointments.
conditions: Deep caries or dental trauma with irreversible pulpitis in primary & permanent teeth

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) For pulpotomy of deciduous and permanent teeth: Restorable tooth crown, teeth with carious or traumatic damage to vital pulps, and teeth without symptoms of irreversible pulpitis, without evidence of pulp tissue degeneration or periapical pathologies. 
2) For indirect pulp capping of deciduous and permanent teeth: Teeth with deep dentinal caries (ICDAS 4, 5, 6) with vital pulp or deep fracture without pulp exposure (max. clinical symptoms of sensitivity to cold and trigger); Radiologically, caries involvement of >70% or 2/3 of the dentin thickness but at least a small dentine bridge, without the presence of periapical pathology, pathological external/internal root resorption, or pulp calcification.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Patients with acute pain/irreversible pulpitis or symptoms requiring further treatment like pulpectomy/root canal treatment/extraction.  
2) Patients with systemic diseases who require special attention during their dental treatment. 
3) Teeth with signs of irreversible pulpitis. 
4) Radiographic signs of internal resorption or pathologic external root resorption and no periapical or interradicular pathologic signs. 
5) Teeth with a history of spontaneous or nocturnal pain, positive percussion, a history of swelling or fistula tracts and teeth without tenderness, physiological or pathological mobility 
6) Allergy to any of the ingredients of the study materials to be used for that specific tooth.
